meaning: a deck-building card game: each turn you play cards from your hand and buy one new card for your deck; most victory points when the game ends wins
the 10 action cards (out of the base set's 26) dealt for one game; with the basic cards they form the supply
the piles of cards on the table that players can buy from
the decision this project learns: which card (or nothing) to add to the deck with this turn's coins
a benchmark bot that buys only treasure and Provinces; Smithy-BM and Witch-BM add one copy or two of that action card
an evolved priority list from dominion-v1 that plays every decision; here it plays all non-buy decisions on both sides
the best portfolio-v2 genome whose required cards are in the kingdom; the opponent of the goal measure
DeepMind's method: a tree search guided by a neural network, and the network trained to predict what the search decided and who won
Monte Carlo tree search: many simulated continuations, each walking down a tree of decisions and backing the result up
one random guess of the hidden information (draw order, opponent's hand), consistent with what the player has seen
the engine function that makes a determinization: it reshuffles everything the buying player cannot see
one walk from the root of the search to a leaf, plus scoring the leaf; 400 per buy here
the rule that picks which buy a simulation tries next: average result so far plus an exploration bonus proportional to the net's prior
the weight of the exploration bonus in PUCT; higher means the search tries buys the net doesn't like more often
the net's probability for each buy, used by PUCT to decide where to look first
divides the net's logits before the softmax; above 1 it flattens a sharp prior so the search explores more
the score given to the position where a simulation stops: here lam × the net's win estimate + (1 − lam) × the result of a GA rollout
finishing a game from the leaf with the GA genome making every decision; one sample of who would win
the mix of net value and rollout at the leaf (0 = rollout only, 1 = net only)
the part of the net that predicts the winner (tanh, +1 win, −1 loss)
the part of the net that gives a probability for each of the 34 possible buys (33 cards + nothing)
how often the search tried each buy at the root; AlphaZero's usual policy target
expert iteration: the net learns the single buy the search chose (one-hot), not the visit shares
Gumbel AlphaZero's target: the prior reweighted by each buy's searched value
Dirichlet noise added to the prior at the root in self-play, so every buy gets tried sometimes
the training data kept: the last 5 iterations' buy decisions
one round of 1,000 self-play games, training on the buffer, and the fixed evaluation
iteration 0: the net trained to copy the GA's buys before any self-play
1,000 games against the GA base on 500 kingdoms never used anywhere else, both seats; the honest number
the 95% confidence interval for a win rate; about ±3 points at 1,000 games
the best of many noisy evaluations is flattered by luck; why "best check" is not the goal number
win = 1, shared win = ½, loss = 0, averaged over games
